blockbuilder.visual_critic_note: Coherent dark dashboard with disciplined monochromatic blue palette and well-structured grid layout, but network node labels render at 9px and are barely legible, and the color scatter panel is dense to the point of being hard to parse without interaction.
blockbuilder.encoding_integrity_note: Both circle-size encodings correctly use scaleSqrt, the timeline bar chart has a zero baseline with a data-driven domain, and the color-view axes use semantically fixed ranges (0–360 hue, 0–100 lightness); the only mild concern is the timeline y-scale freezing at the full-dataset max during filtered updates, which is a context-preservation choice rather than active deception.
flags: Update Storm (partial): bitFilter.set() O(n) bitmask recomputation runs synchronously on every brush mousemove before the RAF guard, hammering the CPU at 60fps
Stale Scale: no window resize handler means x/y scales captured in brush and quadtree closures become stale after layout changes
blockbuilder.stress_test_note: Strong RAF dirty-flag architecture prevents DOM update storms and has no infinite loops or mid-flight transition conflicts, but brush handlers execute expensive O(n) bitset recomputation synchronously on every mousemove event and scales are never refreshed on resize.
blockbuilder.cognitive_load_note: Four linked crossfilter panels with clean monochromatic encoding manage the complexity well — the force network (60 nodes, pre-settled, single blue hue) and HCL color scatter are individually dense but self-describing, and the layout hierarchy (time → network/colors → list) guides attention naturally; the main cost is that users must learn three distinct interaction modes (timeline brush, network click, color brush) before the system clicks.
